context_questions: Who are the primary users and what is the core job they hire the app to do?
What is the single most important user flow for the first release?
What data does the app store, and what are the privacy / auth constraints?

assumptions: users reach the app through a browser
the team can host a backend service and a database
evidence_needs: what conversion or activation metric proves the core flow works
risks: scope creep across too many flows before the core one is validated
auth and data-privacy surface is underestimated
explore.recommended_next_step: prototype the single core flow end-to-end behind a feature flag

acceptance_criteria.text: A new user completes the core flow without reading docs.
Authenticated state survives a page refresh.
The app degrades gracefully when the backend is unreachable.

user_stories: As a first-time visitor, I sign up and complete the core flow in one session.
As a returning user, I land directly in my workspace.
non_goals: No native mobile app in the first release.
No multi-tenant billing in the first release.
risks: the core flow is not validated before secondary features are built
test_implications: an end-to-end test of the core flow

docs_expectations: an API reference for the public endpoints
release_gates: the core-flow e2e is green in CI
